observation.visible_scene: A large white Star Cruises / Genting cruise ship (red-and-blue funnel with a yellow star, lifeboats visible along the port side) is underway in open water, filmed from a rear-quarter aerial angle that shows the stern and the port hull. The backdrop is a coastline with a green hill and high-rise residential blocks on the left and a distant city skyline on the right, under a blue sky with scattered cumulus clouds. A white foamy wake trails behind the stern.
visible_changes: The ship translates forward through the water throughout the excerpt (bow pointing right); it does not rotate or change heading appreciably.

Because the camera tracks the ship and keeps it near the center of frame, the background hill and skyline drift slowly leftward from the first to the last frame, confirming real forward progress of the vessel relative to the shore.
The stern wake churns and re-forms continuously, and the V-shaped wake spreads behind the hull, consistent with steady motion rather than a stationary ship.

The framing changes only slightly: the ship's apparent size is roughly stable with a marginal shift in perspective, indicating the following camera (likely a drone) holds a near-constant rear-quarter position with minor adjustments.
Clouds and water surface show only slow, ambient change; no editing cut or scene transition is visible within the segment.
outside_clip_unknowns: The ship's destination, speed value, and whether it is departing, arriving, or transiting are not shown.
Events before the first frame and after the last frame (the excerpt is a temporal crop with arbitrary endpoints).
The exact camera platform and its full flight path.
uncertain_details: Whether the small change in ship size is due to camera distance or a slight zoom cannot be separated confidently.
The precise magnitude of the ship's speed; only relative motion against the background is observable.
Minor apparent jitter in the horizon line is consistent with handheld/drone camera motion rather than ship roll, but the distinction is not certain.

Observe this actual video clip before reading any existing caption.

Both ends are arbitrary crop boundaries, not the beginning and completion of an action. Motion
may already be underway in the first view and may continue beyond the last. The endpoints need
NOT match or connect as a loop. Do not judge different endpoints as a physical inconsistency,
and do not invent a trigger, contact, start, stop, landing, disappearance or completion to make
the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.
If an editing cut is visible inside the segment, distinguish it from continuous physical motion;
do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.
Describe what is visible during the excerpt, the actual changes, and supported persistent
properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
occlusion, and an already ongoing process from its onset. Only state what the clip supports;
do not invent causes, an earlier impact, an unseen operator, material identities or later outcomes.
Do not infer motion from one frame, a visible seam or a single pose. Static intervals are valid.
Do not supply named physics laws. Compare each important entity's first and last image positions
and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
Return JSON {"visible_scene":"...", "visible_changes":["observation supported within the excerpt"],
"outside_clip_unknowns":["unseen prerequisites or outcomes, only when relevant"],
